[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/26 (Fri) 16:18  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A table was provided showing TCP and UDP details corresponding to the right protocols, including packet requirements and usage scenarios.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) is a connection-oriented protocol that requires the client and the server to establish a connection before sending data.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] TCP is used for applications that require guaranteed delivery of data, such as file sharing and web browsing.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] TCP ensures that all packets are received by the destination and that they are received in the correct order by adding a sequence number to each packet and acknowledging the receipt of each packet.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] If a packet is lost or corrupted, TCP will retransmit the packet until it is successfully delivered.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] UDP (User Datagram Protocol) is a connectionless protocol that does not require the client and the server to establish a connection before sending data.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] UDP is used for applications that do not require guaranteed delivery of data, such as real-time audio and video streaming.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] UDP does not provide the same level of reliability as TCP.
